questions.question: What does using credit allow a borrower to do?
choices: Receive ownership shares without paying
Borrow purchasing power with an obligation to repay
Avoid all future financial obligations
Convert every purchase into tax-free income

questions.question: What is the principal of a loan?
choices: The amount borrowed, excluding interest charges
The lender's annual advertising budget
The borrower's monthly savings target
The total value of the lender's buildings

questions.question: What is interest on borrowed money?
choices: A refund of the original purchase price
The maximum amount a borrower may save
A measure of the borrower's tax bracket
A charge for using the lender's money

questions.question: What does APR stand for in credit agreements?
choices: Average Payment Requirement
Annual Profit Ratio
Annual Percentage Rate
Authorized Purchase Receipt

questions.question: What is a credit report?
choices: A record of credit activity and credit-account history
A monthly list of investment dividends only
A government guarantee that a borrower will repay
A tax form calculating a household's total income

questions.question: What is collateral in a secured loan?
choices: The lender's estimated profit
An asset pledged to back repayment
A fee charged for printing statements
A promise to increase the credit limit

questions.question: What does default mean in a loan agreement?
choices: Repaying the loan ahead of schedule
Transferring money into a savings account
Failing to meet repayment obligations
Increasing the value of collateral

questions.question: Why can making only minimum credit-card payments increase total borrowing costs?
choices: Minimum payments automatically eliminate interest
The card balance becomes a savings deposit
The lender cancels the unpaid principal each month
A balance can remain outstanding longer and accumulate interest

questions.question: Why do lenders examine repayment history?
choices: It helps them assess the likelihood of timely repayment
It guarantees that future income will never change
It determines the borrower's citizenship automatically
It replaces the need to read loan terms

questions.question: How does a debit-card purchase generally differ from a credit-card purchase?
choices: Debit cards always involve long-term borrowing
Debit cards generally draw from account funds rather than a credit line
Credit cards cannot be used for online purchases
Debit cards require collateral for each transaction

questions.question: Why is a lower monthly loan payment not necessarily evidence of a cheaper loan?
choices: Monthly payments never include repayment of principal
All loans have identical repayment periods
A smaller payment always means a lower total balance
A longer repayment period can increase total interest paid

questions.question: Why should a borrower compare fees as well as interest rates?
choices: Fees can be ignored if the loan is secured
Fees are always refunded at the end of a loan
Fees can affect the loan's total cost
Interest rates measure fees in every financial product identically

questions.question: What financial responsibility can a co-signer take on?
choices: Repayment if the primary borrower does not meet the agreement
Ownership of every item the borrower already owns
Authority to change the borrower's tax rate
Freedom from all obligations under the loan

questions.question: Why can borrowing close to a credit-card limit concern lenders?
choices: It proves the borrower has no debt
It may signal heavy reliance on available credit
It guarantees a higher savings balance
It eliminates the importance of payment history

questions.question: Why is checking a credit report useful?
choices: It guarantees approval of every future loan
It lets the borrower remove accurate debts without repayment
It prevents any future identity theft automatically
It can reveal errors or accounts the person did not authorize

questions.question: A one-year loan charges 6% simple interest on $500, with no fees and no payments until year-end. How much interest is owed?
Two loans have the same principal and repayment term, with no fees. One has a lower fixed interest rate. Which generally costs less?
choices: The loan with the lower fixed interest rate
The loan with the higher fixed interest rate
Both must have identical total interest
The loan with the larger initial monthly payment, regardless of rate

questions.question: A card balance is $400. A $100 payment is made, with no new charges, interest, or fees. What balance remains?
A lender offers a small monthly payment but does not mention the loan's length. What information is most important to request next?
choices: The lender's total national advertising budget
The number of years the lender has operated
The repayment term and total cost, including interest and fees
The number of other products offered by the lender

questions.question: A person notices an unfamiliar credit account on their report. Which response best addresses the risk?
choices: Ignore it because account errors cannot affect credit
Borrow more money before anyone reviews the account
Send personal information to an unsolicited caller
Investigate promptly and use official dispute and fraud-reporting channels
